nodes.label: Spectral Anti-Fraud Check — FFT cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1
nodes.community_name: Spectral Anti-Fraud Check — FFT cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1
nodes.norm_label: spectral anti-fraud check — fft cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1
nodes.rationale: Detects MP3s/AAC transcoded up to FLAC — the most common Soulseek fraud — by finding the brick-wall low-pass fingerprint the original lossy encoder imprinted; applies only to P2P-sourced files claiming lossless quality (D3); pure-numpy STFT with async ffmpeg pipe keeps the whole phase ≤3 s per file.

nodes.label: Decision D3 — only P2P lossless-claiming files are spectrally checked
nodes.community_name: Spectral Anti-Fraud Check — FFT cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1
nodes.norm_label: decision d3 — only p2p lossless-claiming files are spectrally checked
nodes.rationale: Fallback streams have known lossy provenance (Opus 128–160k is full-band to ≈20 kHz with no brick-wall cliff), so there is no fraud signal to detect; exempting them avoids wasted analysis on files whose provenance is already honest.

nodes.label: Threat (c) — 16-bit → fake 24-bit
nodes.community_name: Spectral Anti-Fraud Check — FFT cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1

nodes.label: Test fixture suite (7 fixtures, scipy/soundfile recipes)
nodes.community_name: Spectral Anti-Fraud Check — FFT cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1
nodes.norm_label: test fixture suite (7 fixtures, scipy/soundfile recipes)
nodes.rationale: Deviation note (M4): the original Butterworth order-8 recipe rolled off only ≈15 dB at 4 kHz above a 16 kHz cutoff (48 dB/octave) vs the DEAD_MARGIN_DB = 55 rule, drifting to false PASS; real lossy encoders brick-wall (spectrum above cutoff is encoded to zero), so fixtures now use a deterministic raised-cosine mask with a 500 Hz transition band and a hard zero knee. §6 thresholds were not changed; tuning protocol: adjust §6 thresholds, never fixture recipes.

nodes.label: Threat (b) — 44.1 kHz → 96/192 kHz upsample (hi-res void)
nodes.community_name: Spectral Anti-Fraud Check — FFT cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1
nodes.rationale: Content void above 22.05 kHz despite a hi-res claim; v1 emits a soft INCONCLUSIVE flag (rule 5), full FRAUD rule deferred to v2 §9.

nodes.label: Threat (a) — MP3/AAC → FLAC upcast
nodes.community_name: Spectral Anti-Fraud Check — FFT cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1
nodes.rationale: Primary v1 target: hard spectral cutoff at the encoder lowpass (≈16 kHz @128k, ≈18–19 kHz @192k, ≈20–20.5 kHz @320k LAME) with a very steep cliff; accepted limitation — a 320k MP3 upcast cuts at ≈20.5 kHz and passes v1 rules, but is audibly near-transparent; strictness is tunable.

nodes.label: spectral.strict config flag
nodes.community_name: Spectral Anti-Fraud Check — FFT cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1
nodes.rationale: Default: INCONCLUSIVE treated as PASS with a WARNING (lazy pass); when spectral.strict = true an INCONCLUSIVE verdict triggers the fallback instead — trading warned-passes for re-downloads when a lossless claim is doubtful.

nodes.label: Verdict rules v1 (FRAUD / INCONCLUSIVE / PASS), evaluation order
nodes.community_name: Spectral Anti-Fraud Check — FFT cutoff (brick-wall) detector, v1
nodes.norm_label: verdict rules v1 (fraud / inconclusive / pass), evaluation order
nodes.rationale: False-positive containment: steepness gates (f_c ≤ 19 kHz with S ≥ 30 dB/kHz etc.) protect legitimately band-limited recordings (historical transfers, gradual-rolloff classical/mastered content); cost asymmetry — a rare false FRAUD costs one re-download via fallback while a false PASS admits a fake-lossless file — so thresholds deliberately favor rejection within the cliff-evidence regime.
